Bernicia
bur-NISH-uh
n. (the northern Northumbrian kingdom from the Tees to the Forth, with its fortress at Bamburgh)
From a British name, perhaps Bryneich, the land of the passes, latinised by Bede as Bernicia.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Bernicia was the northern half of Northumbria, running from the Tees to the Firth of Forth, with its royal fortress on the basalt rock at Bamburgh above the sea and Lindisfarne in sight of it. Its kings were the dominant English house of the seventh century: Ethelfrith, then Edwin's rival Oswald, who had been baptised in exile among the Scots and who sent to Iona for Aidan in 635, then Oswiu, who settled the Easter question at Whitby in 664. Oswald set up a wooden cross before the battle of Heavenfield and prayed with his army, and Bede makes his reign the beginning of the northern church. The fortress rock and the tidal island together are the geography of the whole story: a king on a crag and a bishop on an island, three miles apart. The dictionary records Bernicia for the figure its fortress supplies. Scripture uses the shelter of a rock and a stronghold constantly for God himself, and it is careful to say that the refuge is a person and not a position, the eternal God and his everlasting arms.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a refuge as shelter from danger; a fortress as a fortified place; a shadow as shade from the sun; to abide as to dwell; and everlasting as lasting for ever.

expand to see more

REFUGE, n. Shelter or protection from danger or distress; that which shelters or protects from danger, distress or calamity.

FORTRESS, n. A fortified place; a large and permanent fortification, sometimes including a town; a fort; a castle.

SHADOW, n. Shade within defined limits; obscurity or deprivation of light; shelter; protection.

ABIDE, v.i. To rest or dwell; to tarry or stay; to continue permanently or in the same state.

EVERLASTING, a. Lasting or enduring for ever; eternal; immortal; perpetual.

Key Scripture

Psa 61:3 — "For thou hast been a shelter for me, and a strong tower from the enemy."

Psa 91:1 — "He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty."

Psa 91:2 — "I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust."

Deu 33:27 — "The eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms: and he shall thrust out the enemy from before thee; and shall say, Destroy them."

Modern Corruption

The northern Northumbrian kingdom from the Tees to the Forth, with its fortress at Bamburgh, whose king Oswald sent to Iona for Aidan in 635.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the refuge Scripture promises is a person. The Psalmist uses exactly the imagery of a Bamburgh: “For thou hast been a shelter for me, and a strong tower from the enemy” (Psa 61:3), and then locates the safety in a dwelling rather than a wall, “He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty” (Psa 91:1).

The live temptation for a warrior kingdom is to confuse the figure with the fortification, and Bernicia's history shows how little the rock could do: Penda besieged Bamburgh and tried to burn it, and the kings of that house died one after another in battle. The Psalmist makes the confession personal and names the object: “I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust” (Psa 91:2). Moses's blessing says the same of a people with no fortress at all, “The eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms” (Deu 33:27).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew machseh (H4268), a refuge; Hebrew metsudah (H4686), a fortress; Hebrew tsel (H6738), a shadow; Hebrew meonah (H4585), a dwelling or refuge.

expand to see more

Hebrew machseh (H4268) — a shelter, a refuge; “thou hast been a shelter for me”, Psalm 61:3.

Hebrew tsel (H6738) — a shadow, shade; “under the shadow of the Almighty”, Psalm 91:1.

Hebrew metsudah (H4686) — a stronghold, a fortress; “He is my refuge and my fortress”, Psalm 91:2.

Hebrew batach (H0982) — to trust, to be confident; “in him will I trust”, Psalm 91:2.

Hebrew meonah (H4585) — a dwelling, a den, a refuge; “The eternal God is thy refuge”, Deuteronomy 33:27.

Usage

"“a strong tower from the enemy” (Psa 61:3) — the figure Bamburgh supplies."

"“He is my refuge and my fortress” (Psa 91:2) — a person, not a crag."

"“underneath are the everlasting arms” (Deu 33:27) — said to a people without walls."
